stem.text: Determine whether the series \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} a_n \), where \( a_n = \frac{2 \left(-1\right)^{n}}{n^{\frac{2}{3}}} \), converges or diverges. Name a test whose conditions the series meets and state the verdict it gives.

answer_key.label: The series converges by the alternating series test, because \( |a_n| \) decreases to 0.

worked_solution.text: The factor \( (-1)^n \) makes the terms alternate, so the alternating series test fits.
worked_solution.rule_named: match the form to a test

worked_solution.text: The absolute values \( \frac{2}{n^{\frac{2}{3}}} \) decrease as n increases, and \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{2}{n^{\frac{2}{3}}} = 0 \).
The series converges by the alternating series test, because \( |a_n| \) decreases to 0.

options.label: The series converges by the nth term test, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} a_n = 0 \).
options.derivation: the verdict drawn from the terms approaching 0 alone, with the alternation and the decrease never used

options.label: The series converges by the alternating series test, because \( |a_n| \) decreases to 0.
The series diverges by the p-series test, because \( p = \frac{2}{3} \le 1 \).
options.derivation: the p-series test named for an alternating series, whose terms are not all positive as that test requires

options.label: The series converges to 0, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} a_n = 0 \).
options.derivation: the limit of the sequence of terms reported as the sum of the series
